text: {"hypotheses":[{"statement":"The ~9 F1 point advantage of the rewrite strategy over naive append is likely driven by reduced cross‑fact interference, as demonstrated in consolidation research; therefore, adding a consolidation/compression step to the append baseline should narrow the performance gap, and an ablation comparing rewrite vs. append+consolidation will isolate the true source of gains.","confidence":0.78,"support_ids":["c0fbabea","5f5331d2","579b3852","03c1d4c1"],"tags":["ablation","memory","consolidation","rewrite"]},{"statement":"The token‑budget overflow observed for the naive append approach by day 20 can be alleviated by incorporating external memory paging (e.g., MemGPT) to offload older context, enabling append‑based agents to operate over longer horizons without exceeding token limits.","confidence":0.65,"support_ids":["c0fbabea","f167ace6","f327063e"],"tags":["token_budget","append","external_memory","MemGPT"]}]}
